memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed the firstborn of
both people and animals in Egypt. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the first
male offspring of every womb and redeem each of my firstborn sons. And it will
be like a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead that the LORD brought
us out of Egypt with his mighty hand." - Ex 13:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The parent's answer continues, and it does not skip the hard part. It names
Pharaoh's stubbornness and it names the death of Egypt's firstborn.

Notice that God does not instruct parents to soften this for children. The
history is told honestly. Faith that only speaks of comfortable things does not
survive contact with real life, and children can sense when they are being told
half a story.

The heart of the answer is this: our sons live because someone died. That is why
we redeem them. Every act of dedication points back to a night of judgment
survived only through a substitute.

There is an honest tension we should not pretend away. God's judgment on Egypt is
sobering, and Scripture does not offer us a tidy explanation that removes all
discomfort. What it does offer is the character of a God who warned repeatedly,
opened a door of escape to anyone, and who ultimately took judgment upon
Himself in His own Son.

That is where this chapter finally points. The Father did give up His firstborn,
and there was no substitute for Him, so that there could be one for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you tell the hard parts of the faith honestly, or only the comfortable
   parts?
2. What does it cost God for you to be free?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You did not spare Your own Son. Help me to hold both Your
holiness and Your mercy without losing either. Amen.
